evidence.supports: Exact tuple and installed 1.7.9b attributes; see identity audit hash.

Installed shared Horf acquisition, normal/hard constants, current-target Shoot event and 20-frame animation; normal-mode controller with explicit local adaptations.

contract.movement: Grounded stationary head. Ordinary movement is zero; native .7 friction/knockback parity remains unfinished.
contract.targeting: Staggered 7-source-frame checks; strict 20-world-unit range and solid line of sight. Current player aim is sampled at Shoot, not fixed at acquisition.
contract.attacks: One physical bullet at Shoot frame 4, speed 21 world units/second, local damage 10 before existing hostile multiplier. Acquisition starts a 28-frame cooldown.
contract.vulnerability: Normally damageable.
contract.phases: 20-frame attack at 30 Hz; full recovery is preserved. Normal mode only. Existing room-entry grace and local stun/capacity policies are explicit adaptations.
contract.offspring: No offspring. Rare Sub Horf replacement is encounter selection, not a death spawn.
contract.completion: Normal room threat; death cancels the cast and counts one kill/reward. No death offspring.
contract.adaptations: Normal-mode source profile: HP 10 x 3.2 = 32; range 200 x .1 = 20 world units; speed 7 per source frame x 30 x .1 = 21 world units/second. Grounded radius .65 and original procedural head appearance remain local adaptations.; Acquisition checks every 7 source frames, strict range and solid line of sight. Attack lasts 20 frames at 30 Hz, Shoot at frame 4, with current player aim. Cooldown 28 starts on acquisition. Floor cooldown multipliers do not modify this source cadence.; Entity ID staggers checks. The actor clock starts from simulation time and pauses while its room is inactive, rather than reproducing native global-frame/index phase on every room visit. Existing room-entry grace is retained; the native 59-frame Appear animation is not reproduced.; Local shot damage 10 receives the existing hostile multiplier once (12.5). Flat 3D shots have a local 5-second lifetime and physical solid collision. Native height, falling and lifetime are not claimed as matched.; A full local event/projectile queue retains the Shoot event and stretches the cast until admission. Stun cancels the cast. These are explicit local policies, not recovered native scheduling or status behavior.; Opening-band ordinary specialists only, matching the Basement analogue. Pursuit/crossfire/supply-guard weights and caps remain local encounter design. Rare Sub Horf replacement stays disabled until that distinct enemy is implemented.
contract.unknowns: Hard/Greedier source cooldown 14 and shot speed 10 are recovered but not enabled: DeathWard currently uses the normal-mode profile. Controlled/charmed targets, champion exceptions, fear/shrink and source status suppression are not fully ported.; Native friction .7 and shared knockback integration, exact animation update order, Appear timing and global acquisition phase across room changes remain unverified or explicitly adapted.; Source projectile vertical trajectory/lifetime and 3D corner, uneven-terrain and low-cover parity require further acceptance. The original local head and warning presentation are retained.; The reviewed rare Sub Horf replacement remains disabled pending its independent reactive attack controller.; Varied-build balance, broader readability and controlled rendered Linux/WASM performance are still open. evidence.supports: Exact installed identity, numeric attributes, zero collision damage and shutdoors false.
Family-specific active/disabled behavior, invulnerability, re-entry and named item/edition exceptions.
Manual per-tuple source contract, positive template routes, inferred versus unknown subtype distinctions and remaining runtime work.
Implemented attack/lifecycle/collision/placement rules, explicit local conversions and remaining named-item/trap dependencies.

contract.movement: Stationary, solid room hazard; no pursuit or ordinary body-contact damage.
contract.targeting: Player position for aimed attacks; orientation-specific hazards retain authored facing.
contract.attacks: Occasional aimed single blood projectile.
contract.vulnerability: Immune to ordinary damage; solid to player movement even with flight. Chaos Card, Little Horn and Euthanasia are documented instant-kill exceptions. Generally respawns on room re-entry after such kills; Stone Eye has a distinct cleared-room re-entry rule. Generic XML HP is not ordinary damageability.
contract.phases: Active until ordinary combat completion or all required pressure plates are pressed; then closes mouth/eyes and stops firing.
contract.offspring: No ordinary enemy offspring. Infestation 2 can create a Blue Spider on an exceptional kill; separate item dependency.
contract.completion: Does not seal doors. Room completion disables shooting without requiring its death; retain the inactive appearance on re-entry.

adaptations.timings: Cadence/windup/speed/damage/laser widths/turn rate and ballistic gravity are explicit local tuning in statues.mechanics, not extracted native AI constants.
adaptations.hp: 20 source HP becomes 64 local HP; 1 source HP becomes 3.2. Ordinary invulnerability makes these bookkeeping values, not standard weapon durability.
adaptations.subtypes: Cross subtype 1 uses an initial diagonal phase as a declared interpretation of the alternate animation name; exact native startup is unverified. Variant 11 never disables in this debug controller; source pressure-plate precedence remains unresolved.
adaptations.placement: Local room chances are 25/30/35 percent in bands 1/2/3. One added hazard is separate from the existing ordinary threat budget. Every proposed footprint must preserve door/objective navigation and avoid roads/river banks; failed proposals are omitted. Generated statues currently receive a hard-coded 1.4-second initial grace before their configured attack cadence; isolated timing fixtures explicitly start with zero cooldown.
adaptations.pressure_plates: Persistent turrets in ordinary combat rooms have an optional deactivation plate. The runtime supports plate-only objectives and objective-free traps, but full new trap-room generation is not enabled here.
adaptations.visuals: Original-style procedural stone bodies, green Vomit stone, triple apertures, fixed-shooter crack and closed inactive face. Body hit boxes and movement footprints use the displayed cube dimensions; these are not source sprites.

contract.movement: Stationary attacks, short in-place hops, and jumps toward the player.
contract.targeting: Cardinal down/side laser triggers; never fires upward.

contract.phases: Two owned eyes detached from start. Green form replaces short/long-hop rings with two/three arcing explosive shots, uses green creep and summons two Chargers on large-creep action.
contract.offspring: Owns two Bloat Eyes; green form also summons ordinary Chargers with separate summon ownership.
contract.completion: Boss defeat removes its eyes and pays the encounter reward exactly once.

adaptations.hp: Bloat 450*3.2=1440; normal Charger 20*3.2=64. Invulnerable eye HP remains the local sentinel 1, not a source HP conversion.
adaptations.damage: Bloat contact 20, beams/shots/creep/eye/Charger contact 10, green blast 20 before hostile multiplier1.25. Starting player remains100 HP/24 damage.

adaptations.lasers: Fixed world south corresponds to source down; two parallel front rays or opposed side rays from sockets. Range32/radius.32/duration.7/recovery1.5/alignment.8 are local. Geometry is clipped at creation; solid cover also guards damage. No added telegraph delay.
adaptations.creep: Large radius3, landing radius1, lifetime6. Nearby owned deposits refresh rather than unbounded stacking. Large creep action summons ordinary independent Chargers; they survive body death and must be cleared for room completion.
adaptations.ipecac: 1.1s aimed flight, gravity12, lateral spread2, explosion radius2.8/damage20; discrete swept 3D motion and flat-plane fallback only without canyon terrain. adaptations.charger: Local dash11 before1.1 movement multiplier, maximum1.5s, alignment.8, recovery.7, wander timers.7..1.8; no anticipation windup. Native exact speed/timer/stop conditions require measurement.
adaptations.selection: Bands2/3 native weight6, Bloat normal3/green1. These weights are local, not source spawn odds. Dedicated stream leaves layout/ordinary selection RNG independent.

records.name: Stone Eye

evidence.supports: Exact installed identity, numeric attributes, zero collision damage and shutdoors false.
Family-specific active/disabled behavior, invulnerability, re-entry and named item/edition exceptions.
Manual per-tuple source contract, positive template routes, inferred versus unknown subtype distinctions and remaining runtime work.
Implemented attack/lifecycle/collision/placement rules, explicit local conversions and remaining named-item/trap dependencies.

contract.movement: Stationary, solid room hazard; no pursuit or ordinary body-contact damage.
contract.targeting: Clockwise rotating beam heading rather than player pursuit.
contract.attacks: Continuously rotating, flickering Technology laser.
contract.vulnerability: Immune to ordinary damage; solid to player movement even with flight. Chaos Card, Little Horn and Euthanasia are documented instant-kill exceptions. Generally respawns on room re-entry after such kills; Stone Eye has a distinct cleared-room re-entry rule. Generic XML HP is not ordinary damageability.
contract.phases: Active rotating laser until room clearance; do not import Repentance+ full-turn-before-first-shot behavior.
contract.offspring: No ordinary enemy offspring. Infestation 2 can create a Blue Spider on an exceptional kill; separate item dependency.
contract.completion: Does not seal doors; stops firing on clear and disappears after the cleared room is exited and re-entered.

adaptations.timings: Cadence/windup/speed/damage/laser widths/turn rate and ballistic gravity are explicit local tuning in statues.mechanics, not extracted native AI constants.
adaptations.hp: 20 source HP becomes 64 local HP; 1 source HP becomes 3.2. Ordinary invulnerability makes these bookkeeping values, not standard weapon durability.
adaptations.subtypes: Cross subtype 1 uses an initial diagonal phase as a declared interpretation of the alternate animation name; exact native startup is unverified. Variant 11 never disables in this debug controller; source pressure-plate precedence remains unresolved.
adaptations.placement: Local room chances are 25/30/35 percent in bands 1/2/3. One added hazard is separate from the existing ordinary threat budget. Every proposed footprint must preserve door/objective navigation and avoid roads/river banks; failed proposals are omitted. Generated statues currently receive a hard-coded 1.4-second initial grace before their configured attack cadence; isolated timing fixtures explicitly start with zero cooldown.
adaptations.pressure_plates: Persistent turrets in ordinary combat rooms have an optional deactivation plate. The runtime supports plate-only objectives and objective-free traps, but full new trap-room generation is not enabled here.
adaptations.visuals: Original-style procedural stone bodies, green Vomit stone, triple apertures, fixed-shooter crack and closed inactive face. Body hit boxes and movement footprints use the displayed cube dimensions; these are not source sprites.

contract.unknowns: Exact native projectile speed, firing interval/selection, collision shape and effect-specific status/timing exceptions are not established. Pressure plates and ordinary re-entry now have concrete runtime tests. Named instant-kill/reroll/on-hit items and special re-entry exceptions remain unfinished. Named Dead Eye and Fire Mind projectile-hit behavior must be preserved despite ordinary invulnerability.

placement.note: One optional navigation-validated hazard, separate from kill-required enemies.

behavior.scope: Aimed/triple/ballistic volleys; actual explosion; first-tick clockwise flickering laser; fixed stream and Brimstone attacks; cardinal/diagonal alternation and explicit always-on phase policy; ordinary immunity; last actual foe triggers clear; retained inactive solids; plate objectives and persistent optional turrets; all plates required; immediate beam shutdown; re-entry and exceptional respawn without ordinary kill rewards; walking/flight/swept dodge/mouse navigation and actual projectile collision.

reachability.scope: Eight independent source-backed hazard identities occur in legal generated combat rooms; one optional hazard at most, separate from ordinary 4–14 actor budget. Persistent turrets get reachable optional plates; failed geometry placement is omitted. Both variant-11 always-on forms remain debug-only pending dedicated trap routing. No new hazards in band 0, the tutorial or Mine route.

visual_linux.scope: Original-style stone bodies retain closed inactive faces, green Vomit stone and a visible rotating laser. Pressed plates turn teal; emitted projectiles retain their ordinary lifetime after shutdown. The actual seed 0/floor 3/room 8 view shows a turret and plate alongside five ordinary threats. Foreground canyon walls still obstruct some isolated views; procedural faces depend on viewing direction and a floor grate overlaps the seeded turret footprint visually. These captures are partial presentation evidence, not all-camera readability or human difficulty acceptance.

visual_wasm.scope: Exact identity has an isolated attack/lifecycle capture in the complete 81-case run. The two persistent turrets also have real seeded-room captures. Remaining all-camera presentation and balance gates are open.

performance.scope: Structural bounds only: one optional hazard per combat room, 120 candidate placements and 32 plate candidates, shared actor/projectile/hazard limits. Collision-list reconstruction scans resident actors each tick; no controlled current-roster Linux/WASM frame-time signoff.

unresolved: Chaos Card, Euthanasia, Little Horn, Infestation 2, Dead Eye, Fire Mind and D10-specific behavior need real item/effect producers; generic damage/death hooks are not those item implementations.
Cross Grimace bombed-door early-deactivation quirk and variant 11 plate precedence remain unverified/unimplemented. Variant 11 requires dedicated trap routing before gameplay reachability acceptance.
Vomit replacement probability/context, native random shot intervals, exact projectile/laser dimensions, hitbox and phase timings remain unmeasured.
Gaping Maws, Quake Grimaces and Bomb Grimace supply/dedicated encounter dependencies remain source-only.
Mixed-room balance, all-camera readability and controlled Linux/WASM performance acceptance remain open.

contract.movement: Form a circular group that rotates rapidly while the group moves toward the player. Preserve member slots as flies die.

contract.adaptations: Shared controller replaces legacy independent orbits. Local tuning: ring radius 2.4 world units, angular speed 2.6 rad/s, center speed 1.4 (existing global 1.1 multiplier), assembly speed 8; source establishes maximum ten members. Stable entity-order initial groups; dead angular slots remain vacant. Arrivals fill vacancies or bisect the largest gap without shifting survivors. Whole-circle flight clearance and independent member elevations adapt 2D flight to canyons; impossibly narrow rooms use individual pursuit until a valid circle is available. Four-fly ordinary encounters cost three threat points. Source HP 5 is still locally tuned to 32 and not a universal conversion.

evidence.supports: Exact installed identity, numeric attributes, zero collision damage and shutdoors false.
Family-specific active/disabled behavior, invulnerability, re-entry and named item/edition exceptions.

contract.movement: Stationary, solid room hazard; no pursuit or ordinary body-contact damage.
contract.targeting: Attracts player and both friendly and hostile projectiles toward its position.
contract.attacks: No shot emission; suction changes player movement and projectile trajectories.
contract.vulnerability: Immune to ordinary damage; solid to player movement even with flight. Chaos Card, Little Horn and Euthanasia are documented instant-kill exceptions. Generally respawns on room re-entry after such kills; Stone Eye has a distinct cleared-room re-entry rule. Generic XML HP is not ordinary damageability.
contract.phases: Active suction; pressure plates can deactivate it.
contract.offspring: No ordinary enemy offspring. Infestation 2 can create a Blue Spider on an exceptional kill; separate item dependency.
contract.completion: Does not seal doors; pressure-plate deactivation is documented, automatic ordinary combat-clear deactivation is not established.

adaptations.hp: Source 100 HP becomes 320 under the existing 3.2 conversion; ordinary invulnerability makes it bookkeeping, not weapon durability.
adaptations.forces: Normal peak player speed 2 units/s and projectile acceleration 12 units/s²; Broken 4 and 24. Range 24 units with linear falloff, vertical extent 4 units and projectile planar speed limit 40. Existing shots faster than the limit keep their incoming speed ceiling. These are local 3D values, not extracted Isaac constants.
adaptations.multiple_fields: Vectors sum and oppose each other, capped at the strongest participating configured peak. This local cap preserves movement counterplay and bounded acceleration; exact native stacking is unknown.
adaptations.collision: Player displacement is swept against ordinary world geometry and statue solids. Forces do not operate in corridors or inactive rooms. Physical input and aim remain under existing controls; stand-still does not cancel suction.
adaptations.cycle: Broken begins in its active half and alternates every four seconds. Cycle pauses while the room is inactive and resumes on return. Four-second period is sourced; startup phase and offscreen persistence are declared adaptations pending native measurement.
adaptations.visuals: Existing Original-style stone body with a larger dark mouth, Broken cracks and four small inward-moving dust motes; inactive phase closes the mouth. No source art imported.
adaptations.configuration: Forces, extents, cycle and pool weights are external. A current expedition retains its immutable content snapshot after edits.

contract.unknowns: Exact native force/attenuation/height/stacking and initial or inactive-room phase behavior remain unknown. Named item exceptions need real producers. Pressure plates, swept player motion, both projectile factions and re-entry now have concrete partial implementation.

placement.note: Optional source-band hazard with a reachable pressure plate; actual generated routes verified in the current 170-floor regression.

behavior.scope: Actual idle/keyboard/dodge/mouse/stand-still player movement; stronger Broken force; zero shot emission/contact damage/room threat; four-second on/off boundaries and resumed cycle; ordinary-clear persistence; actual plate contact and permanent shutdown; inactive-room phase persistence; exceptional kill/respawn without ordinary kill rewards; real projectile acceleration for both teams; stopped acceleration after plate contact; vertical bounds and preserved ballistic gravity; wall/corridor bounds; cancellation and bounded stacking; file-only force change and immutable snapshot.

reachability.scope: Both Maws occur in real seeded source-backed bands 1–3, with a reachable optional pressure plate and retained ordinary companions. The 170-floor regression reaches ten hazard identities, preserves 29 ordinary/conditional identities, mandatory routes, the four bands and unchanged room/threat budgets. No Maw enters opening-band, tutorial or Mine pools.

performance.scope: Structural bounds only: active fields cached per simulation step; one optional hazard per generated combat room; configured aggregate peak/speed and existing actor/projectile limits. No controlled native/WASM current-roster performance acceptance.

records.name: Movable TNT

evidence.supports: Installed exact tuple and numeric attributes.
Source-edition family behavior; Repentance+ additions are excluded.
Exact Hornfel passenger table, mounted carrier lifetime and special damage/destruction preflight. No linear-HP hazard port is certified.

contract.movement: Pushable solid TNT moved by player/enemy contact.
contract.targeting: No AI target.
contract.attacks: Explodes on destruction; ignites against flame, spiked rock or red dung.
contract.vulnerability: Tears, blasts and stomp effects; unlike fixed TNT, invulnerability contact and Hagalaz do not destroy it.
contract.phases: Intact, pushed, detonated; no generic enemy attack cycle.
contract.offspring: No enemy offspring; destruction creates one blast.
contract.completion: Not a room threat; remove blocking collision after explosion.
contract.adaptations: Use separate environmental/dedicated encounter routing, never normal enemy weights; preserve original Western visual style and player defaults.
contract.unknowns: Unspecified native timing, force and probability thresholds require measurement or documented tuning.

placement.note: Two environmental payloads available; five unported creature choices consume an attempt without substitute.

behavior.scope: 58 native suites including real projectile durability, fire/TNT batches, flame ignition, queue retention, pushing, quiet rail exit and room-clear/re-entry lifecycle.

reachability.scope: Actual unforced environmental passenger arrivals in seeded Standard Broken Quarry. Ordinary environmental dressing/item-created TNT are not enabled.

visual_linux.scope: Original native renderer. Procedural distinct fire/TNT on separate carrier; no complete camera/readability matrix.

visual_wasm.scope: Six actual WASM cases, errors[], ground spent states and two natural transport routes; full regression not rerun.

unresolved: Implement push/contact collision, ignition, destruction chain limits and distinct Mine Crafter cube appearance.
Mine Crafter item-created routing must be separate from natural obstacle placement.
Audit remaining source damage/status/loot callbacks; supported flame/basic explosive paths do not establish all native exceptions.
Full ordinary placement, varied-build/human balance and rendered Linux/WASM performance acceptance remain open.
implementation_notes: Normal fire per-hit durability and TNT per-batch durability, source no-threat role, quiet mounted exits, distinct destruction and persistent ground remnants. World scale/contact/push/clock are documented local adaptations.
Source loot callbacks, all item/status exceptions and other environmental variants remain open. No completed port.

records.name: Leper

evidence.supports: Installed Repentance 1.7.9b exact tuple, attributes and subtype identity; linked audit retains XML hash.
Reviewed family/variant behavior sections. Later Repentance+ notes are excluded from baseline unless separately identified.

contract.movement: Alternate approaching and fleeing until the last head stage; at 15 source HP continuously chase and leave red damaging creep.
contract.targeting: Player position; head-loss thresholds track cumulative damage rather than one chunk per hit.
contract.attacks: Contact damage after the documented head-loss stage; detach one Leper Flesh for each crossed 15-HP threshold.
contract.vulnerability: Normal damage; source contact-state image needs a precise stage mapping.
contract.phases: Start at 60 source HP / corresponding missing head chunks. Preserve later thresholds even on large hits.
contract.offspring: Final death leaves Leper Flesh and 50% grey Gusher. Post-hit HP <= -25 suppresses only Gusher, not Flesh.
contract.completion: Parent and detached hostile parts are separate room threats.
contract.adaptations: Retain DeathWard player defaults and original visual style. World-unit movement, collision radii, attack timing and existing tuned HP are provisional conversions, not measured Isaac constants.
contract.unknowns: Exact native timers, acceleration and unspecified selection weights remain unmeasured. Champion/status/item interactions and source stageHP conversion require separate verification.

placement.note: Source presence proposes a stage; no pool activation or parity approval is implied.

unresolved: Implement threshold-crossing damage hooks, head stages and detached parts.
Resolve contact-state boundary and final chunk duplication on a lethal threshold crossing.
Verify all six completion gates and unresolved source/DeathWard conversion details.

records.name: Quake Grimace

evidence.supports: Exact installed identity, numeric attributes, zero collision damage and shutdoors false.
Family-specific active/disabled behavior, invulnerability, re-entry and named item/edition exceptions.
Manual per-tuple source contract, positive template routes, inferred versus unknown subtype distinctions and remaining runtime work.
Concrete directional landing/wave implementation, source-backed band and declared adaptations; partial validation attached.

contract.movement: Anchored hop/landing action; no horizontal pursuit.
contract.targeting: Installed animation filename specifies left; other coordinate/arena conventions still need explicit mapping.
contract.attacks: On landing, creates a directional line of rocks; source cadence three seconds. The attack can break a secret/super-secret wall in its path.
contract.vulnerability: Immune to ordinary damage; solid to player movement even with flight. Chaos Card, Little Horn and Euthanasia are documented instant-kill exceptions. Generally respawns on room re-entry after such kills; Stone Eye has a distinct cleared-room re-entry rule. Generic XML HP is not ordinary damageability.
contract.phases: Repeated landing attacks normally continue after ordinary combat ends; pressure plates can deactivate it.
contract.offspring: No ordinary enemy offspring. Infestation 2 can create a Blue Spider on an exceptional kill; separate item dependency.
contract.completion: Does not seal doors. Ordinary clear generally does not stop its attack; plate completion does.

adaptations.coordinates: Installed left/up/right/down animation suffixes map to fixed -X/-Z/+X/+Z. Subtypes never turn toward the player or room center.
adaptations.cycle: Source three-second landing cadence; local startup waits a full cycle. Hop occupies the last 0.45 seconds, reaching one world unit high. Inactive rooms pause phase. Physical stationary footprint remains solid during cosmetic lift.
adaptations.wave: Local moving front speed 10 units/s, radius 0.5, range 32, base damage 10 (12.5 after the unchanged 1.25 hostile multiplier) and 0.5-second visual trail. One hit per front; trail is cosmetic. Wave is planar at ordinary actor height, clipped at terrain and room boundaries. Ordinary enemies are not targets; vulnerable allied companions use their existing shared contact cooldown.
adaptations.barriers: Source attack opens secret/super-secret entrances. DeathWard currently has an optional cache enclosure, not the full Isaac secret-room graph. CacheGate is the explicit local entrance analogue: one wave opens it and pays its existing seeded reward once. CrackedRock also breaks, a local adaptation. OreSeam, CacheSide and structural terrain stay intact. Wave stops on its first solid surface even when that surface breaks; cover is evaluated before destruction. No inventory bomb is spent or explosion/ordinary-kill credit awarded.
adaptations.plate: Pressure plates stop further hops/landings. A previously emitted wave finishes its finite course, like other emitted attacks. Exact source plate interaction with in-flight rocks remains unmeasured.
adaptations.placement: Separate one-hazard budget, source-backed band 1 only, fixed inward-facing axis with at least six clear travel units and optional reachable plate. Existing room/ordinary-threat budgets unchanged.
adaptations.visuals: Original procedural stone head, broad brow/directional wedge, anchored hop and travelling low-poly rock crest. No source art or map style changes.

contract.unknowns: Exact native projectile speed, firing interval/selection, collision shape and effect-specific status/timing exceptions are not established. Pressure plates, instant-kill items, reroll behavior, re-entry and projectile-hit item hooks need concrete runtime support and tests.

placement.note: Actual source-band-1 route verified in 170-floor regression, fixed axis and usable lane, reachable plate, independent hazard budget.

behavior.scope: All four fixed axes; no horizontal pursuit; actual hop before three-second landing; three-second repeat period; moving front at configured speed; real player damage through existing multiplier; one hit per front; airborne/cover/corridor protection; first-surface demolition independent of prop order; cache reward once and intact bomb inventory/kill/explosion accounting; persistent opened geometry; ordinary-clear and plate/re-entry policy; inactive phase pause; hazard-cap suppression; file-only speed edit and snapshot isolation.

reachability.scope: All four directional Quakes found in real band-1 generated rooms, with fixed inward axes, usable attack lane, optional reachable plate and retained ordinary residents. The 170-floor regression reaches fourteen separate hazard identities and preserves ordinary room/threat budgets. No Quake opening/tutorial/Mine entries.

visual_linux.scope: Native hop/wave/resident captures and four-axis browser captures inspected in Original style. Broad brow, directional wedge, short fixed-axis chevrons and moving low-poly crest are visible. The first capture revealed a generic warning aimed at an unset target; replaced with short directional arrows. Low contrast against sand and HUD/scenery overlaps still need all-camera readability review. Screenshot FPS is not a controlled performance measurement.

visual_wasm.scope: Four isolated directional variants and four actual generated rooms; all-camera readability not accepted.

balance.scope: Deterministic grounded/airborne/cover contacts preserve player defaults and existing 1.25 hostile impact multiplier; this is not human or varied-build encounter balance acceptance.

performance.scope: Structural bounds: one optional hazard per generated room, existing global hazard cap, finite wave duration and bounded seven-piece visual trail. No controlled native/WASM current-roster benchmark acceptance.

unresolved: Full secret/super-secret-room routing is not implemented by the cache analogue.
Source-exact wave speed, hit radius, damage conversion, hop timing/height, first-cycle phase, geometry interactions and lifetime require measurement.
Named instant-kill, reroll, Infestation 2, Dead Eye and Fire Mind item producers remain dependencies.
All-camera visual readability, mixed-build/human balance and controlled native/WASM performance acceptance remain open.
